public_body: Advisory Board Of The Berkshire Regional Transit Authority
overall: Board violated the OML by posting an insufficiently specific notice for its September 25 meeting; the October 30 discussion did not cure it. No intentional violation found. Board members ordered to complete training.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice for the September 25 meeting, listing 'Administrator Search Update', was not sufficiently specific. Board argued an October 30 vote cured any violation.
allegations.key_passage: By the time of the September 25 meeting, the Board was moving on to the next stage of hiring Kathleen Lambert as the new Administrator, contract negotiations.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued the notice violation was intentional. AG found no prior warning on the specificity requirement and rejected the other intent arguments.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we cannot say that the Board was previously warned to include greater specificity in meeting notices, the requirement at issue here.

allegations.summary: Not raised in complaint: AG noted the Board excluded a person from an open session, took a secret ballot, referred to candidates by code, and minutes lacked interview summaries.
allegations.key_passage: A meeting is not truly open to the public when members speak in code.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
All Board members must attend an Open Meeting Law training webinar provided by the AG's office within 90 days of the letter and certify completion to the office.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
